verses.sanskrit:
युधिष्ठिर उवाच।
              चातुराश्रम्यमुक्तं ते चातुर्वर्यं तथैव च। राष्ट्रस्य यत्कृत्यतमं ततो ब्रूहि पितामह॥१॥
verses.english: Vyasa said O excellent son, accosted by you. I have told you truly what the answer to your question should be according to the doctrine of Knowledge as explained in the Sankhya system.

verses.sanskrit:
भीष्म उवाच।
              राष्ट्रस्यैतत्कृत्यतमं राज्ञ एवाभिषेचनम्। अनिन्द्रमबलं राष्ट्रं दस्यवोऽभिभवन्त्युत॥२॥
verses.english: Listen now to me as I explain to you all that should be done according to the Yoga doctrine. The unison of intellect and Mind, and all the Senses, and the all-prevading Soul is said to be the highest kind of knowledge. That Knowledge should be gained by one who is of a tranquil mind, who has governed his senses, who is capable of seeing the Soul, who takes pleasure in (such) meditation, who is gifted with intelligence and purity in acts. One should try to gain this knowledge by abandoning those five obstacles of Yoga which are known to the wise, namely, desire, anger, cupidity, fear, and sleep. Anger is conquered by tranquility of disposition. Desire is defeated by giving up all purposes.

verses.sanskrit: अराजकेषु राष्ट्रेषु धर्मो न व्यवतिष्ठते। परस्परं च खादन्ति सर्वथा धिगराजकम्॥३॥
verses.english: By meditating with the help of the understanding upon topics deserving meditation one, gifted with patience, succeeds in relinquishing sleep. By steady endurance one should govern his organs of generation and the stomach. One should protect his hands and feet by his eyes.

verses.sanskrit: इन्द्रमेव प्रवृणुते यद्राजानमिति श्रुतिः। यथैवेन्द्रस्तथा राजा सम्पूज्यो भूतिमिच्छता॥४॥
verses.english: One should protect his eyes and ears by the help of his mind, and his mind and speech by his acts, One should avoid fear by carefulness, and pride by attending the wise.

verses.sanskrit: नाराजकेषु राष्ट्रेषु वस्तव्यमिति रोचये। नाराजकेषु राष्ट्रेषु हव्यमग्निर्वहत्युत॥५॥
verses.english: Controlling procrastination, one should by these means subdue these obstacles of Yoga. One should pay his adorations to fire and the Brahmanas and should bow his head to the gods.

verses.sanskrit: अथ चेदाभिवर्तेत राज्यार्थी बलवत्तरः। अराजकाणि राष्ट्राणि हतवीर्याणि वा पुनः॥६॥
verses.english: One should avoid all kinds of unholy conversation and malicious speech and words which pain other minds. Brahma is the effulgent seed. It is again, the essence of that seed from which proceeds all this.

verses.sanskrit: प्रत्युद्गम्याभिपूज्यः स्यादेतदत्र सुमन्त्रितम्। न हि पापात्परतरमस्ति किञ्चिदराजकात्॥७॥
स चेत्समनुपश्येत समग्रं कुशलं भवेत्। बलवान्हि प्रकुपितः कुर्यान्निःशेषतामपि॥८॥
verses.english: Brahma became the eye, in the form of this mobile and immobile universe, of all elements that were born. Meditation, study, gift, truth, modesty, simplicity, forgiveness, purity of body, purity of conduct, and subjugation of the senses, these increase one's energy which dissipates his sins.

verses.sanskrit: भूयांसं लभते क्लेशं या गौर्भवति दुर्दुहा। अथ या सुदुहा राजन्नैव तां वितुदन्त्यपि॥९॥
verses.english: By treating impartially all creatures and by living contentedly upon what is gained easily and without exertion one acquires the fruition of all his objects and succeeds in gaining knowledge.

verses.sanskrit: यदतप्तं प्रणमते नैतत्संतापमर्हति। यत्स्वयं नमते दारु न तत्संनामयन्त्यपि॥१०॥
verses.english: Purged of all sins, gifted with energy, sparing in diet, with senses under complete control, one should, after having subdued his desire and anger, try to attain to Brahima.

verses.sanskrit: एतयोपमया वीर सन्नमेत बलीयसे। इन्द्राय स प्रणमते नमते यो बलीयसे॥११॥
verses.english: Uniting firmly the senses and the mind with gaze fixed inwards, one should, in the silent hours of evening or those before dawn, fix his mind upon the understanding.

verses.sanskrit: तस्माद्राजैव कर्तव्यः सततं भूतिमिच्छता। न धनार्थो न दारार्थस्तेषां येषामराजकम्॥१२॥
verses.english: If even one of the five senses of a human being be kept ungoverned all his wisdom escapes through it like water through a hole not made up at the bottom of a leather bag.

verses.sanskrit: प्रीयते हि हरन्पापः परवित्तमराजके। यदास्य उद्धरन्त्यन्ये तदा राजानमिच्छति॥१३॥
verses.english: The mind in the first instance should be controlled by the Yogin like a fisherman trying at the commencement to make that one among the fish powerless from which he auticipates the greatest danger to his nets. Having first governed the mind, the Yogin should then proceed to subdue his ears, then his tongue, and then his nose.

verses.sanskrit: पापा ह्यपि तदा क्षेमं न लभन्ते कदाचन। एकस्य हि द्वौ हरतो द्वयोश्च बहवोऽपरे॥१४॥
verses.english: Having controlled these, he should fix there on the mind. Then withdrawing the mind from all purposes. He should settle it on the understanding.

verses.sanskrit: अदासः क्रियते दासो ह्रियन्ते च बलात्स्त्रियः। एतस्मात्कारणाद्देवाः प्रजापालान्प्रचक्रिरे॥१५॥
verses.english: Indeed having governed the five senses, the Yati should fix them on the mind. When these with the mind for the sixth become concentrated in the understanding, and thus centred remain steady and firm then Brahma becomes perceptible like a smokeless blazing fire or the effulgent Sun.

verses.sanskrit: राजा चेन्न भवेल्लोके पृथिव्यां दण्डधारकः। जले मत्स्यानिवाभक्ष्यन्दुर्बलं बलवत्तराः॥१६॥
verses.english: Indeed, one then beholds in himself his own soul like lightning in the firmament. Everything then appears in it and it appears in cverything on account of its infinitude.

verses.sanskrit: अराजकाः प्रजाः पूर्वं विनेशुरिति नः श्रुतम्। परस्परं भक्षयन्तो मत्स्या इव जले कृशान्॥१७॥
verses.english: Those great Brahmanas, who are possessed of wisdom, who are endued with fortitude, who are possessed of high knowledge and who are cngaged in the well being of all creatures, succeed in saying it.

verses.sanskrit: समेत्य तास्ततश्चक्रुः समयानिति नः श्रुतम्। वाक्शूरो दण्डपरुषो यश्च स्यात्पारजायिकः॥१८॥
यः परस्वमथादद्यात्त्याज्या नस्तादृशा इति। विश्वासार्थं च सर्वेषां वर्णानामविशेषतः। तास्तथा समयं कृत्वा समयेनावतस्थिरे॥१९॥
सहितास्तास्तदा जग्मुरसुखार्ताः पितामहम्। अनीश्वरा विनश्यामो भगवन्नीश्वरं दिश॥२०॥
verses.english: Acquiring by Yoga annihilation, extension, power to present different shapes in the same person or body, celestial scents, and sounds, and sights, the most agreeable sensations of taste and touch, pleasurable sensations of coolness and warmth, equality with the wind, power to understanding the meaning of scriptures and every work of genius, living with celestial damsels, the Yogin should not care for them and merge them all in the Understanding.

verses.sanskrit: यं पूजयेम सम्भूय यश्च नः प्रतिपालयेत्। ततो मनुं व्यादिदेश मनुर्नाभिननन्द ताः॥२१॥
verses.english: Restraining words and the senses should practise Yoga after dusk and before dawn seated on a mountain summit, or at the foot of a huge tree or with a tree before him.

verses.sanskrit: मनुरुवाच। बिभेमि कर्मणः पापाद्राज्यं हि भृशदुस्तरम्। विशेषतो मनुष्येषु मिथ्यावृत्तेषु नित्यदा॥२२॥
verses.english: Controlling all the senses within the heart, one should, with faculties concentrated, think on the Eternal and Indestructible like a man of the world thinking of wealth and other valuable properties. One should never, while practising Yoga, with draw his mind from it. one

verses.sanskrit:
भीष्म उवाच।
              तमब्रुवन्प्रजा मा भैः कर्तॄनेनो गमिष्यति। पशूनामधिपं चाशद्धिरण्यस्य तथैव च॥२३॥
verses.english: One should with devotion pursue those mcans by which he may control the restive mind. One should never suffer himself to fall away from it.

verses.sanskrit: धान्यस्य दशमं भागं दास्यामः कोशवर्धनम्। कन्यां शुल्के चारुरूपां विवाहेषूद्यतासु च॥२४॥
मुखेन शस्त्रपत्रेण ये मनुष्याः प्रधानतः। भवन्तं तेऽनुयास्यन्ति महेन्द्रमिव देवताः॥२५॥
verses.english: With the senses and the mind withdrawn from everything else, the Yogin should repair 10 empty caves of mountains, to temples consecrated to the gods and to empty houses or apartiments, for living there.

verses.sanskrit: स त्वं जातबलो राजा दुष्प्रधर्षः प्रतापवान्। सुखे धास्यसि नः सर्वान्कुबेर इव नैर्ऋतान्॥२६॥
verses.english: One should not mix with another in either speech, act or thought. Disregarding all things and eating very sparingly the Yogin should regard equally objects acquired or lost.

verses.sanskrit: यं च धर्मं चरिष्यन्ति प्रजा राज्ञा सुरक्षिताः। चतुर्थं तस्य धर्मस्य त्वत्संस्थं वै भविष्यति॥२७॥
verses.english: He should treat equally one who praises and one who censures him. He should not seek the good or the evil of one or the other.

verses.sanskrit: तेन धर्मेण महता सुखं लब्धेन भावितः। पाह्यस्मान्सर्वतो राजन्देवानिव शतक्रतुः॥२८॥
verses.english: He should not rejoice at an acquisition or be sorry at a failure or loss. Treating all beings equally he should imitate the wind.

verses.sanskrit: विजयाय हि निर्याहि प्रतपन् रश्मिवानिव। मानं विधम शत्रूणां जयोऽस्तु तव सर्वदा॥२९॥
verses.english: Brahma, represented by sound, appcars very clearly unto one whose mind is thus turned to itself, who leads a pure life, and who sees all things equally, indeed unto one who is ever engaged in Yoga thus for even six months.

verses.sanskrit: स निर्ययौ महातेजा बलेन महता वृतः। महाभिजनसम्पन्नस्तेजसा प्रज्वलन्निव॥३०॥
verses.english: Seeing all men stricken with anxiety the Yogin should regard a clod of earth, a piece of stone, and a lump of gold with an equal eye. Indeed, he should withdraw himself from this path, cherishing a hatred for it, and never allow himself to be stupefied.

verses.sanskrit: तस्य दृष्ट्वा महत्त्वं ते महेन्द्रस्येव देवताः। अपतत्रसिरे सर्वे स्वधर्मे च ददुर्मनः॥३१॥
verses.english: By following the path indicated above, even a person of an inferior caste, or a woman, will surely acquire the highest end.

verses.sanskrit: ततो महीं परिययौ पर्जन्य इव वृष्टिमान्। शमयन्सर्वतः पापान्स्वकर्मसु च योजयन्॥३२॥
एवं ये भूतिमिच्छेयुः पृथिव्यां मानवाः क्वचित्। कुर्यू राजानमेवाग्रे प्रजानुग्रहकारणात्॥३३॥
verses.english: He who has subdued his mind sees in his own self, by the help of his own understanding the Increate, Ancient, Undeteriorating, and Eternal Brahma,-That which cannot be attained to except by controlled senses,-That which is subtler than the most subtile, and grosser than the most gross, and which is Emancipation's self.

verses.sanskrit: नमस्येरंश्च तं भक्त्या शिष्या इव गुरुं सदा। देवा इव च देवेन्द्रं तत्र राजानमन्तिके॥३४॥
verses.english: Bhishma said By ascertaining from the preceptors and by themselves reflecting with their minds upon these words of the great Rishi spoken so properly wise persons become at one with Brahima himself, till, indeed, the time when the universal dissolution sets in that swallows up all existent beings.

verses.sanskrit: सत्कृतं स्वजनेनेह परोऽपि बहु मन्यते। स्वजनेन त्ववज्ञातं परे परिभवन्त्युत॥३५॥
verses.english: One who is respected by his own people becomes an object of esteem with his enemies also, while one who is disregarded by his own is set at naught by enemies.

verses.sanskrit: राज्ञः परैः परिभवः सर्वेषां स सुखावहः। तस्माच्छत्रं च पत्रं च वासांस्याभरणानि च॥३६॥
verses.english: If the king be disregarded by his enemies, all his subjects become unhappy. Therefore, umbrellas, vehicles, external ornaments, foods, drinks, palaces, seats, beds, and all utensils for use and show, should be dedicated to the king.

verses.sanskrit: कृतज्ञो दृढभक्तिः स्यात्संविभागी जितेन्द्रियः। ईक्षितः प्रतिवीक्षेत मृदु वल्गु च सुष्ठु च॥३९॥
verses.english: Grateful, firmly devoted, and with subdued passions, he should give to others their due. Eyed by others, he should look at them mildly, sweetly, and beautifully.

verses.sanskrit: भोजनान्यथ पानानि राज्ञे दद्युर्गृहाणि च। आसनानि च शय्याश्च सर्वोपकरणानि च॥६७॥
गोप्ता तस्माद्दुराधर्षः स्मितपूर्वाभिभाषिता। आभाषितश्च मधुरं प्रत्याभाषेत मानवान्॥६८॥
verses.english: By such means, the king will better discharge his duties of protection and become irresistible. He should always smilingly be spoken to by others and he should speak to others sweetly.
